title: Hydrophilic Coating ‹ Teleflex Medical
body_text: New Hydrophilic Coating Technology from Teleflex Medical OEM Wayne, PA Teleflex Medical OEM, a recognized global leader in catheters, introducers, and delivery systems, announces a proprietary, hydrophilic surface coating for polymer-based devices that are navigated through the vascular system. The coating performs favorably in terms of lubricity and extended durability when compared to other coatings on the market. It has proven biocompatibility and shelf-life stability. It also exhibits low particulate count in testing, and outstanding adhesion to the substrate material. The coating can be customized to optimize certain performance characteristics based on specific user needs. Similar to other hydrophilic coatings, Teleflex Medical OEM’s coating may reduce the required insertion force which may result in improved control, placement, and tracking of a device. Applications for this surface technology include introducers, diagnostic catheters, balloon catheters, and components. The coating is applied through a fully-automated process in a temperature and humidity controlled cleanroom. Teleflex Medical OEM’s extensive, in-house capabilities enable medical devices to be engineered, manufactured, and coated under one roof. This vertical integration can reduce the complexity, and the development and commercialization time often encountered in launching new devices. Pega was recognized as a Leader among 13 vendors Gartner evaluated for Completeness of Vision and Ability to Execute across multiple criteria, including Offering (Product) Strategy, Innovation, Product/Service, Customer Experience, and Operations, among others. Last year this report was published as Gartner Magic Quadrant for Process Mining Platforms 2025, for which Pega was also named a Leader. The evaluation also included Pega Process Mining and Pega Task Mining, which provide visibility into how processes run across systems and how work is actually performed. By feeding mined insights directly into Pega Blueprint, organizations can simulate and optimize processes, then automatically convert them into reimagined workflows and applications – accelerating transformation from discovery to tangible outcomes. title: Flow Traders Selects CoreWeave for Model Training
summary: Flow Traders selected CoreWeave as its primary AI cloud platform to power high-intensity foundation model training for AI-driven quantitative trading.
body_text: LIVINGSTON, N.J. -- July 28 -- CoreWeave , Inc. (Nasdaq: CRWV), The Essential Cloud for AI™, today announced that Flow Traders, a leading global liquidity provider, selected CoreWeave as the primary AI cloud platform provider for its AI and deep learning division. The agreement marks Flow Traders’ migration of high-intensity training workloads to CoreWeave Cloud. As quantitative trading firms build out dedicated AI and deep learning divisions, foundation model training has become a core competitive discipline rather than a side project. These workloads demand consistent multi-node performance at scale, a requirement that has pushed firms like Flow Traders to move beyond general-purpose clouds toward AI-native platforms built for frontier-scale trading. “ Tomorrow's innovations can't be built on yesterday's infrastructure,” said Joshua Mathew, co-head of Flow Traders’ recently announced AI and deep learning division. “We are committed to conducting cutting edge research to model financial markets, and our partnership with CoreWeave secures the technology and scale that is required for it.” Under the agreement, Flow Traders has secured dedicated compute capacity to support the training of foundation models at the core of its AI-driven quantitative trading strategy. Flow Traders selected CoreWeave following a competitive evaluation that highlighted CoreWeave’s multi-node performance, a critical factor for the large-scale, high-intensity training workloads that define frontier model development in quantitative finance, along with CoreWeave’s technical support and roadmap planning. “Flow Traders is one of the financial services firms pushing the boundaries of what’s possible with AI-driven trading, and that requires a platform that doesn’t buckle under multi-node, high intensity,” said Jon Jones, chief revenue officer at CoreWeave. “We built CoreWeave Cloud to deliver consistent performance at scale, and we’re proud to support Flow Traders’ AI and deep learning division as it moves these models toward production.” CoreWeave was selected for its ability to deliver the cluster-level performance and reliability that AI-driven trading strategies demand, combined with an integrated software and support layer that helps teams move from training models to production applications and agents with confidence. As Flow Traders prepares to go live with its AI and deep learning division, CoreWeave's platform provides the technical foundation to support that launch and the growth expected to follow. CoreWeave consistently delivers industry-leading performance, demonstrated by record-breaking MLPerf benchmark results , its position as the only AI cloud to earn the top Platinum ranking in both SemiAnalysis ClusterMAX™ 1.0 and 2.0, and its #1 ranking for inference speed and price-performance for Moonshot AI’s Kimi K2.6 in independent inference benchmarking conducted by Artificial Analysis.

title: Gemini: 950 millones de usuarios y 3 modelos | Coderhouse
summary: Gemini alcanza 950 millones de usuarios y lanza tres modelos nuevos. Qué cambia para quienes usan IA en el trabajo y cuál conviene según el caso.
body_text: Dan Patiño AI Strategy & Innovation en Coderhouse Inteligencia Artificial Gemini llega a 950 millones de usuarios y lanza tres nuevos modelos: qué cambia para quienes usan IA en el trabajo Publicado el 23 de julio de 2026 Google confirmó que su app Gemini alcanzó los 950 millones de usuarios mensuales y lanzó tres nuevos modelos, según los resultados financieros del segundo trimestre presentados el 22 de julio. El dato importa más allá de la cifra: marca cómo se está consolidando el ecosistema de IA y qué implica para quienes ya la usan como herramienta de trabajo. Para el profesional promedio, la pregunta no es cuántos usuarios tiene Gemini, sino qué modelo conviene usar según cada tarea y cómo aprovechar mejor este crecimiento acelerado. Vamos a lo concreto. Los números detrás del anuncio En su reporte de resultados, la CEO de Alphabet destacó que la app Gemini llegó a 950 millones de usuarios activos mensuales y que sus usuarios diarios se triplicaron en el último año, según recogió Forbes . El contexto financiero acompaña: los ingresos de Alphabet crecieron 24% interanual y Google Cloud aceleró su crecimiento hasta 82%, impulsado por la demanda de infraestructura de IA. Ese crecimiento del negocio en la nube no es un detalle: muestra que las empresas están adoptando IA a un ritmo que sostiene la inversión en más y mejores modelos. Los tres nuevos modelos Junto con las cifras, Google presentó tres nuevos modelos de Gemini. Entre ellos se destacó una variante especializada en seguridad, diseñada para detectar y corregir vulnerabilidades de software, disponible por ahora solo para gobiernos y socios de confianza a través de un piloto de acceso limitado, según TechCrunch . La lógica detrás de tener varios modelos es clara: no existe un modelo único que sea óptimo para todo. Google —igual que sus competidores— apuesta por una familia de modelos donde cada uno equilibra de forma distinta velocidad, costo y capacidad de razonamiento. Cuál conviene usar según el caso Aunque los nombres comerciales cambian seguido, el criterio para elegir se mantiene estable. Como regla general: Tareas rápidas y de alto volumen (resumir, clasificar, responder correos): conviene un modelo "flash" o liviano, más veloz y económico. Razonamiento complejo (análisis, código, planificación): conviene el modelo más capaz de la familia, aunque sea más lento o caro. Tareas con documentos largos: priorizá los modelos con ventana de contexto amplia, que pueden "leer" mucho texto de una vez. Casos especializados (seguridad, dominios técnicos): buscá si existe un modelo específico, que suele rendir mejor que uno general. El aprendizaje práctico es no usar siempre el modelo más potente "por las dudas": elegir el adecuado ahorra tiempo y dinero. Si querés ampliar tu caja de herramientas más allá de Gemini, revisá nuestra selección de herramientas de IA para la productividad laboral . Qué implica para el ecosistema en la región La escala de Gemini tiene efectos concretos para quienes trabajan en LATAM. Por un lado, la competencia entre Google, OpenAI, Anthropic y otros empuja los precios hacia abajo y la calidad hacia arriba: los usuarios ganan. Por otro, la integración cada vez más profunda de Gemini en herramientas que ya usás —correo, documentos, planillas— baja la barrera de entrada: no hace falta ir a una app aparte para aprovechar la IA. El riesgo es la dependencia. Cuando una sola familia de modelos se vuelve omnipresente, conviene mantener criterio propio: saber cuándo la IA acierta, cuándo conviene verificar y cómo no atarse a un único proveedor. Ese criterio es hoy una habilidad profesional en sí misma. Cursos recomendados de Coderhouse Para pasar de usuario ocasional a alguien que aprovecha la IA con criterio, este recorrido ayuda según tu nivel: Si querés entender qué hay detrás de modelos como Gemini, el Curso de Introducción a la Inteligencia Artificial te da la base conceptual. Para sacarle el máximo a estos modelos en tareas diarias, el Curso de Generación de Prompts te enseña a pedirle bien a la IA. Y para integrar estos modelos en flujos de trabajo automáticos, el Curso de AI Automation conecta la IA con tus procesos. La IA ya es parte del trabajo: elegí el programa que te dé el criterio para usar el modelo correcto en cada tarea. Preguntas frecuentes ¿Cuántos usuarios tiene Gemini? Google informó 950 millones de usuarios activos mensuales de la app Gemini en sus resultados del segundo trimestre presentados el 22 de julio, y señaló que sus usuarios diarios se triplicaron en el último año. ¿Qué modelos nuevos lanzó Google? Presentó tres nuevos modelos de Gemini, entre ellos una variante especializada en seguridad para detectar y corregir vulnerabilidades de software, disponible inicialmente solo para gobiernos y socios de confianza en un piloto de acceso limitado. ¿Qué modelo de IA conviene usar para cada tarea? Para tareas rápidas y de alto volumen, un modelo liviano y veloz; para razonamiento complejo, el más capaz de la familia; para documentos largos, uno con ventana de contexto amplia. Usar siempre el modelo más potente no es eficiente en tiempo ni en costo. ¿Este crecimiento de Gemini me afecta si uso otra IA? Sí, indirectamente. La competencia entre proveedores empuja precios más bajos y mejor calidad para todos, y la integración de la IA en herramientas cotidianas baja la barrera de entrada, uses el proveedor que uses. ¿Conviene depender de un solo proveedor de IA? No es recomendable atarse por completo. Mantener criterio propio —saber cuándo verificar los resultados y poder cambiar de herramienta— es una habilidad profesional clave para no quedar rehén de un único ecosistema. Sobre el autor Dan Patiño Soy Dan Patiño, responsable de AI Strategy & Innovation en Coderhouse. Mi día a día consiste en fusionar la gestión táctica del e-commerce (CRO, Email Marketing y SEO) con el desarrollo de soluciones disruptivas. Me especializo en crear apps internas con IA para automatizar tareas y potenciar la innovación dentro del equipo. Creo fielmente que la tecnología es el mejor aliado de la estrategia. Para profundizar en mi recorrido profesional, te espero en mi perfil de LinkedIn.

title: Cash Book for MSMEs
summary: Explore what a cash book is, its types, key benefits, and how digital cash book software like GimBooks simplifies bookkeeping, GST compliance, and financial management.
body_text: Why Do MSMEs Need a Cash Book? A cash book is one of the most important financial records for an MSME. It tracks every rupee coming in and going out, helping business owners stay in control of their cash flow, avoid errors, and make informed decisions. Here are the key reasons: 1. Know Your Cash Position Anytime Many MSMEs struggle because they don't know how much cash is actually available. A cash book provides a real-time view of: Cash in hand Money received Money spent Current cash balance 2. Prevent Cash Shortages Businesses often fail due to poor cash flow rather than lack of profits. A cash book helps you: Track daily expenses with digital billing expense software for MSME Plan upcoming payments Ensure enough funds for salaries, rent, and suppliers 3. Avoid Missing Transactions Small cash expenses can easily go unnoticed. Recording every transaction helps: Reduce accounting mistakes Prevent duplicate entries Minimize chances of fraud or cash leakage 4. Simplify GST & Tax Filing A well-maintained cash book makes it easier to: Reconcile accounts Prepare financial statements Support GST return filing Provide records during audits 5. Improve Business Decisions Knowing where money is being spent helps owners: Cut unnecessary expenses Allocate budgets better Invest in profitable areas 6. Build Better Financial Discipline Daily cash recording creates a habit of financial accountability and keeps business records organized. 7. Track Customer Collections A cash book helps verify: Which customers have paid How much cash was received Whether payments match invoices How to track customer collections with GimBooks digitally. 8. Monitor Business Growth Comparing monthly cash inflows and outflows helps identify: Sales trends Seasonal fluctuations Business growth over time 9. Prepare for Loans Banks and financial institutions often ask for financial records before approving loans. An updated cash book ledger demonstrates: Healthy cash management Organised business records Financial credibility 10. Save Time with Digital Accounting Instead of maintaining manual registers, digital cash books: Automatically record transactions Generate reports instantly Reduce calculation errors Sync with invoices, expenses, and bank entries Read more: How to maintain ledger for business. Common Problems MSMEs Face Without a Cash Book Running out of cash despite good sales Losing track of daily expenses Difficulty reconciling accounts Errors during GST filing Unclear profit and cash position Missed customer payments Poor budgeting and planning How GimBooks Cash Book Helps MSMEs Ban and cash ledger With GimBooks, MSMEs can: Record cash received and paid instantly Track real-time cash balance Manage income and expenses in one place Generate financial reports automatically Keep business records organised for GST filing Access cash book data anytime from mobile or desktop A digital cash book removes the need for manual bookkeeping and gives business owners better visibility into their finances, helping them make faster and more informed decisions. SPONSORED Explore free cashbook billing tool for MSME Download now Conclusion cash book is more than just a record of daily transactions—it's a tool that helps MSMEs maintain financial control, improve cash flow, and make informed business decisions. Whether you're managing a retail store, service business, or manufacturing unit, keeping an accurate cash book reduces errors, simplifies accounting, and prepares your business for GST compliance, audits, and future growth. With a digital cash book like GimBooks, you can record every transaction in real time and manage your business finances from anywhere. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) 1. What is a cash book? A cash book is a financial record that tracks all cash receipts and cash payments of a business. It helps maintain an accurate record of daily cash transactions and cash balance. 2. Why is a cash book important for MSMEs? A cash book helps MSMEs monitor cash flow, avoid cash shortages, reduce accounting errors, simplify GST filing, and make better financial decisions. 3. What is the difference between a cash book and a cash account? A cash book serves as both a book of original entry and a ledger account, whereas a cash account is only a ledger account prepared from journal entries. 4. What are the different types of cash books? The three main types are: Single Column Cash Book Double Column Cash Book (Cash and Bank) Triple Column Cash Book (Cash, Bank, and Discount) 5. Can I maintain a cash book digitally? Yes. Accounting software like GimBooks allows you to maintain a digital cash book with automatic calculations, real-time updates, and financial reports. 6. Is a cash book mandatory for small businesses? While maintaining a specific cash book format isn't mandatory for every business, keeping accurate records of cash transactions is essential for proper accounting, taxation, and financial management. 7. How often should a cash book be updated? Ideally, a cash book should be updated immediately after every cash transaction or at least at the end of each business day. 8. Does a cash book help with GST filing? Yes. A properly maintained cash book makes it easier to reconcile transactions, prepare financial statements, and support accurate GST return filing. 9. Can a cash book track both cash and bank transactions? Yes. A double-column or triple-column cash book records both cash and bank transactions, making it easier to manage overall business finances. 10. Which is the best cash book app for MSMEs? The best cash book app should offer real-time transaction recording, expense tracking, bank reconciliation, reporting, and GST-ready accounting. GimBooks provides all these features in a simple, mobile-first accounting solution for MSMEs.

title: SafeBase vs Conveyor vs Skypher for Security Reviews (2026)
summary: How SafeBase (Drata), Conveyor, and Skypher compare on trust centers, questionnaire automation, portal coverage, and answer control for security reviews.
body_text: ‍ TL;DR SafeBase is a dedicated trust center, now owned by Drata. Strong on access control and buyer-facing portal design. Questionnaire automation runs through a Chrome extension with limited portal coverage and a token-based usage cap. Conveyor is a vendor security review platform with named AI agents (Sue for questionnaires, Phil for access reviews). Backed by $39M in funding and 750K+ questions analyzed. Questionnaire automation is credit-based, with ~8 fully automated portal integrations and no PDF round-trip. Skypher is questionnaire automation built for every format buyers actually send, with a trust center on the same knowledge base. 40+ portal integrations, answer style control, self-maintaining knowledge base. Adobe, Deel, and McKinsey are customers. Where the comparison gets interesting is what happens after the trust center. Portals deflect routine requests. They do not complete the 200-question Excel file or the SIG Lite a buyer sends anyway. What SafeBase, Conveyor, and Skypher were built for SafeBase, Conveyor, and Skypher each started from a different problem, and that origin still shows in the product. ‍ SafeBase started as a trust center: a branded portal where prospects self-serve SOC 2 reports, policies, and certifications behind access controls and NDA workflows. Drata acquired it for $250 million in February 2025, making SafeBase the trust center layer inside Drata's compliance platform. Questionnaire automation came later. Conveyor started as a vendor security review platform. Its AI agents, Sue (questionnaires) and Phil (access reviews), handle inbound security assessments and power a trust center. Conveyor has analyzed 750K+ security questions across its customer base, giving it a proprietary dataset few competitors match. ‍ Skypher started as questionnaire automation. The product was built around the reality that 71.2% of security questionnaires arrive as Excel, 19.2% through online portals, and 9.6% as Word documents (from 100,000+ questions processed). The trust center came second, built on the same knowledge base that powers questionnaire responses. ‍ How SafeBase handles security reviews after the Drata acquisition SafeBase's trust center offers document access segmentation by buyer type, per-account analytics showing who viewed which report, configurable Salesforce routing, and Ironclad NDA integration. Security teams get granular control over who sees what. For teams whose primary goal is a polished, analytics-rich portal that deflects routine requests, SafeBase does that job well. ‍ The questionnaire side is thinner. SafeBase's Chrome extension suggests responses for OneTrust, Panorays, Google Forms, and a handful of other portals. Anything outside that list means exporting to Excel, running it through the platform, and manually entering answers back into the portal. G2 reviewers flag inconsistent AI answer quality: some report answers that are too short and lack detail, while others describe output that requires trimming. The knowledge base requires manual maintenance, which SafeBase's own blog acknowledges can lead to "duplicates, conflicts, and outdated answers." ‍ Questionnaire volume is token-based. If an upload goes wrong, it burns a token. One G2 reviewer describes the system as "only feasible for long questionnaires to be efficient in token use." Companies running multiple products sometimes end up managing three or four separate trust portals inside SafeBase. The platform supports multi-product setups, but G2 reviewers note that trust center templates are "quite rigid" with limited customization. ‍ The Drata acquisition adds a question at renewal. Pricing is custom-quoted across three tiers with no published figures, and third-party analysis from April 2026 notes that "Drata has not publicly committed to pricing stability for existing SafeBase standalone customers." ‍ How Conveyor's AI agents handle security questionnaire automation Conveyor drafts answers through Sue, its questionnaire AI agent, pulling from a knowledge base of policies, past responses, and connected sources (Google Drive, Confluence, Notion). Phil handles access review workflows separately. The product is well-funded ($39M raised, 63 employees) and claims 95%+ first-pass accuracy. G2 reviewers report real-world accuracy closer to 75% after extended use, with AI-generated responses that "require manual fine-tuning." ‍ Portal automation is tiered. About eight portals (ServiceNow, OneTrust, BitSight, ProcessUnity, Coupa, LogicGate, Venminder, UpGuard) are fully automated. Five more support page-level automation through a browser extension, one page at a time. Everything else falls back to a generic AI scan. PDFs cannot be exported back to PDF format; uploads are converted to Word tables. Teams whose buyers require responses in the original PDF have an extra manual step. ‍ The knowledge base uses a Q&A pair architecture. It stays static until someone manually updates it. Connected external sources sync once per week, not in real time. Conveyor recommends maintaining 200 to 400 curated Q&A pairs and acknowledges that more than that "is unrealistic to keep up-to-date." ‍ Pricing is credit-based, starting at $9,600/year for the Professional tier with 10 RFP project credits. High-volume teams "hit credit limits mid-quarter and either slow down responses or pay for top-ups," according to G2 reviewers. ‍ The trust center supports custom domains and document sharing. Multiple reviewers describe customization as limited, particularly around branding and layout. NDA-protected document access is priced per access, which adds up for teams with large customer bases. ‍ How Skypher handles security questionnaire automation and trust centers Skypher processes questionnaires in every format buyers send: Excel, Word, PDF, and 40+ online portals including OneTrust, ServiceNow, Archer, Ariba, and Coupa. No format conversion. PDFs go back as PDFs. ‍ Answer style is configurable per questionnaire . Short Answer gives one-line responses with no extra detail. Precise Answer scopes tightly to the question with no adjacent context. Custom Prompt lets teams write their own instruction for tone, length, and what to include or leave out. Same knowledge base, different output. ‍ The knowledge base is self-maintaining. Documents, previous questionnaire responses, and connected sources update automatically without manual tagging or Q&A pair curation. Above a configurable confidence threshold, the system reuses previously approved answers verbatim instead of reformulating through generative AI. No unnecessary rewriting of language a reviewer already signed off on. ‍ Customer names in questionnaire responses are anonymized through data masking before being sent to any LLM provider. One customer's name never appears in another customer's questionnaire. Skypher's trust center includes NDA gating, Salesforce and HubSpot CRM integration (with auto-approval for existing customers), Slack notifications for access requests, and a buyer-facing AI agent that answers questions about published documents directly in the portal. Multi-product setups run within a single instance. Migration support includes bulk import of existing customer access lists, so switching providers does not disrupt the buyer experience. ‍ Adobe processes over 3,000 questionnaires a year through Skypher. Response time went from two weeks to two hours. Accuracy across 200+ enterprise customers: 96%. ‍ Trust center features compared across SafeBase, Conveyor, and Skypher Feature SafeBase (Drata) Conveyor Skypher Custom domain Yes Yes Yes NDA gating Yes (Ironclad integration) Yes (priced per access) Yes (included) Access control by buyer type Granular segmentation Basic Configurable CRM integration Salesforce Limited Salesforce + HubSpot Auto-approve existing customers Yes (via Salesforce) No Yes (via CRM logic) Buyer analytics Per-account, detailed Basic Per-account Multi-product support Yes (rigid templates) Limited Yes Buyer-facing AI agent No No Yes Slack access request notifications No No Yes Trust center customization Rigid templates (G2) Limited (G2) Configurable Security questionnaire automation features compared Feature SafeBase (Drata) Conveyor Skypher Excel support Yes (.xlsx, .xlsm) Yes Yes Word support Yes (.docx) Yes Yes PDF support Limited Upload only (exports as Word) Full round-trip Portal integrations Chrome extension (limited range) ~8 fully automated, ~5 page-level 40+ Answer style control No No Yes (Short, Precise, Custom Prompt) Knowledge base maintenance Manual (tagging, auditing) Manual (200-400 Q&A pairs, weekly sync) Self-maintaining Verbatim answer reuse No No Yes (above confidence threshold) Source citations Varies Not guaranteed Every answer Data masking Not specified Not specified Yes (customer names anonymized) Volume limits Token-based Credit-based Fixed annual volume commitment Pricing model Custom-quoted, tiered From $9,600/yr, credit-based Volume-based, unlimited users ‍ The widest gaps are portal coverage, answer control, and knowledge base maintenance. SafeBase and Conveyor both require manual knowledge base upkeep and use per-use pricing where credits or tokens can run out mid-quarter. Skypher's self-maintaining knowledge base and fixed annual pricing give teams a predictable cost from day one across the full range of formats and platforms buyers use. FAQ Can SafeBase, Conveyor, or Skypher replace each other as trust center software? All three include a trust center, but depth varies. SafeBase has the most mature access control and buyer analytics. Skypher adds a buyer-facing AI agent and Slack approval workflows. Conveyor's trust center is functional but reviewers describe customization as limited. Where these platforms really diverge is how they handle the questionnaires buyers still send after visiting the portal. How do SafeBase and Conveyor handle security questionnaires submitted through online portals? SafeBase uses a Chrome extension that supports a limited set of portals (OneTrust, Panorays, Google Forms, and others). For unsupported portals, teams export questions to Excel, process them, and manually re-enter answers. Conveyor fully automates about eight portals and offers page-level browser extension support for five more. Skypher integrates with 40+ portals including OneTrust, ServiceNow, Archer, Ariba, and Coupa. What happens to existing customer access when switching trust center providers? Teams with hundreds of customers who already have trust center access need a migration path that does not disrupt the buyer experience. Skypher supports bulk import of existing customer access lists and CRM-based auto-approval, so previously approved buyers keep access without re-requesting or re-signing NDAs. SafeBase migration requires re-populating the evidence library and re-configuring access controls. Conveyor's NDA-per-access pricing model means re-granting access at scale has a direct cost impact. Does Skypher support multi-product trust centers? Yes. Companies selling multiple products or managing trust portals inherited through acquisitions can run them within a single Skypher instance. Each product has its own documentation, knowledge base entries, and access controls. The questionnaire automation module can answer for multiple products simultaneously, including questions that span both. How do SafeBase, Conveyor, and Skypher compare on pricing? SafeBase pricing is custom-quoted across three tiers (Foundation, Advanced, Enterprise) with no published figures. Third-party estimates place starting prices around $15,000/year, with questionnaire automation using a token system. Conveyor starts at $9,600/year with credit-based questionnaire and RFP project limits. Skypher prices based on annual questionnaire volume with a fixed upfront commitment for the contract term, and includes unlimited users with no per-seat fees. All three require a conversation with sales for final pricing. ‍ ‍

title: How to Set Up Automated Recurring Payments for Online Services?
summary: Manage subscriptions, recurring billing, and payments with SubscriptionFlow.
body_text: How to Set Up Automated Recurring Payments for Online Services? Jul 20th, 2026 by Julie John Recurring Billing Share Subscriptions are among the most promising ways to ensure predictable, recurring revenue for an online business. However, running subscriptions is not as easy as it seems. The foundational step in establishing a successful subscription model is to set recurring payments , a process that goes far beyond simply charging a customer’s card once at a set interval. When handled manually, it is more of an administrative hassle than a growth engine. This makes setting up an automated recurring system an absolute necessity. Automating your recurring payment solves problems on both sides of the equation. It promises predictable cash flow for your business and offers convenience to customers. But to achieve automation, you need a setup that handles variable pricing, protects customer data, recovers failed transactions, and scales with your revenue. How Recurring Payments Work In simple words, recurring payments involve charging your customers at a predefined interval. This can be weekly, monthly, quarterly, or annually. In the modern recurring payment ecosystem, there are three core modules in setting up recurring payments: the payment gateway, subscription management engine, and customer interface (also known as checkout). A payment gateway works as the financial building block. It stores payment details, verifies available funds, and transfers the payment to the merchant’s account. While payment gateways process payments, they are unable to manage subscription lifecycles. This is where the subscription management engine comes in. It is responsible for all other complexities involved in recurring payments, including intricate subscription lifecycles. It also controls when and how to charge. Customer interference, on the other hand, is where your subscriber interacts with your billing system. It includes a hosted checkout page and a self-service portal where subscribers can view their current plans, access payment history, and update info. To manage these three well, there’s a need for a centralized revenue engine that can automate your entire billing workflow without the need to administer them separately. Why Businesses Need Automated Recurring Payments Undoubtedly, automation brings convenience. But for subscription businesses, it is more of a necessity than an add-on. Predictable Cashflow Primarily, it brings predictability. Automatic payments make it easier to forecast revenue and help businesses make informed decisions. This gives teams confidence, which aids in exploring new revenue generation streams. Reduced Churn Another promising output of automating recurring payments is reduced churn. Most subscription cancellations are not intentional. They occur due to expired cards, insufficient funds, and fraud-prevention blocks, etc. Automated systems have built-in retry logic and dunning management issues that helps recover failed payments capturing lost revenue. Less Manual Work Managing repeated tasks manually are time taking and error-prone. Someone gets double-charged, someone gets missed entirely, or some invoices go out with the wrong amount. This not only increases administrative burden but also hurts business’s integrity. Higher Customer Retention By automating the entire subscription lifecycle , businesses offer additional convenience for customers and avoid service interruptions. This improves customer satisfaction and ultimately leads to a higher customer retention rate. You have done your part. Let SubscriptionFlow take it from here! Let us help your business grow with our powerful subscription management software. Schedule a Demo Step-by-Step Guide to Automate Recurring Payments Step 1: Define your Subscription Plans and Pricing Models The first step is deciding how to bill your users. Automated billing systems handle several billing models. Flat-Rate Billing : A fixed amount is paid for utilising a product or accessing a service irrespective of the usage. Tiered Billing: Define different rates for individual quantity brackets. Users can upgrade or downgrade the layer based on use. Volume-Based Pricing: Set a single, discounted per-unit rate for the entire purchase when the customer subscribes to the highest quantity bracket Usage-Based Billing : Bill customers on the basis of exact consumption, such as API calls made, gigabytes stored, or active contacts managed Hybrid Billing: Combine flat-rate subscriptions with usage-based charges, customizing plans for customers. After mapping your billing logic, define your billing cadences (monthly, quarterly, monthly). Step 2: Ensure Data Security and PCI Compliance After deciding how to bill, you need to store the customer’s card info to charge them on an ongoing basis. For this purpose, there’s a need to strictly follow security and regulatory compliance. For this purpose, businesses need to follow the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS), which governs how card data needs to be handled. It binds businesses not to store the raw card numbers on their own servers. Instead, rely on tokenization to store data. In tokenization, the processor encrypts the card details at entry and assigns a token that can be used for future charges without ever touching the actual card number again. If you’re selling internationally, additional regional rules are applied to ensure data security: Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) and 3D Secure: It is required across Europe, adding a verification step (like a one-time code) during setup to counter fraud. Tax Compliance: VAT, GST, and local sales tax need to be calculated based on the geographical location of the subscriber. Step 3: Integrate Your Payment Gateways and Billing Software When logic and compliance are sorted, connect your tech stack. Select Payment Gateways: Don’t restrict yourself to a single payment method. Offer a variety of options, including credit card, debit card, ACH, online transfer via PayPal, Apple Pay , etc. When customers see their preferred payment method, the conversion rate increases. Connect to Your Billing Engine: Link your selected payment gateways to your subscription management platform using secure API keys or native integrations. Set Up Product Catalogs: Build out your product catalog, create your plans, add add-ons, and establish discount rules within the billing engine. Step 4: Design Frictionless Checkout Pages and Customer Portals Checkout is the final step when a potential customer turns into a subscriber. Therefore, it is important to keep this process clean and transparent. Keep the fields short and minimal, collecting essential information like name, email, payment info, and billing address. State the renewal terms plainly, including amount, interval, and renewal date. Vague billing terms lead to chargebacks and erode customer trust. After ensuring frictionless checkout, the next step is to certify that customers have a self-service portal. Once someone’s subscribed, they should be able to manage their own account. Self-service portals let customers: Update card details Download past invoices Switch tiers Pause or cancel subscription Step 5: Automate, Proration, Invoicing, and Lifecycle Events Subscriptions are rarely static. People upgrade mid-cycle, add seats, and pause for a few weeks. If you’re calculating these changes manually, you eventually end up making costly mistakes. Therefore, there’s a need for a well-built system that can handle this automatically. Every successful charge should generate an invoice and receipt without anyone having to click a button. And webhooks should tie your billing engine to your actual application. If a payment fails or a plan expires, access is modified or revoked without manual intervention. Step 6: Implement Smart Dunning Management Use an effective dunning strategy to retry payments. This includes processing retries at strategic times to increase the success rate. Send a friendly, direct email pointing to a secure link where the customer can update their card without logging in anywhere. Many billing platforms also sync with card networks directly, so an expired or reissued card updates in the background with no outreach needed at all. Additionally, introduce grace periods and pauses. This gives the retry login time to work while keeping the customer relationship intact. Common Mistakes to Avoid While automating your recurring billing, avoid these common mistakes to ensure a successful setup. Not testing the full billing cycle : Businesses usually test only the initial signup and forget the rest. This often leads to unsolved problems at the time of upgrade, checkout, or cancellation. Ignoring failed payment recovery: Make sure that your system has retry logic to recover failed payments. This is often where the most preventable churn happens. Overcomplicating pricing plans: Avoid offering too many tiers and add-ons. This confuses customers and makes billing logic harder to deal with. Not making cancellation easier: It’s important to offer a convenient exit strategy. This even attracts more customers as it builds more trust and reduces voluntary churn because customers don’t feel trapped. How SubscriptionFlow Can Subscription Flow Help? Setting up automated recurring payments for online services involves too many fragmented systems. You need to choose a gateway, handle tokens securely, map out billing logic, build dunning management, stay compliant across regions, and keep an eye on churn-related metrics. Managing all these manually or relying on disconnected tools is possible, but not feasible for long-term growth. This is exactly the gap SubscriptionFlow fills. It is a dedicated subscription management and billing automation platform that handles flexible billing cycles, proration, and multi-currency support out of the box. Here’s what makes SubscriptionFlow stand out: Pricing and Billing Flexibility Run your suitable plans, such as flat-rate, seat-based, usage-metered, and hybrid, etc., from one interface and change your pricing strategy without rebuilding your codebase around it. True Gateway Independence SubscriptionFlow connects with major global payment gateways , including Stripe, Authorize.net, Ayden, Peach Payments, iyzico, etc., giving you complete freedom over your payment processing architecture. AI-Powered Revenue Recovery The dunning engine handles retries and customer outreach automatically, typically recovering the revenue that is otherwise lost due to involuntary churn. Complete Subscription Lifecycle Control From self-service portals and customizable checkouts to multi-currency, global tax support, and real-time revenue analytics (MRR, ARR, Churn, CLTV), all sit in one dashboard instead of five different tools. If you’re evaluating how to build or improve your recurring billing process, it’ s worth looking at a platform purpose-built for this exact task.
